messages.subject: Interaction of xlim() adn y limits set by facet_wrap(...,scales="free_y")
messages.subject_clean: Interaction of xlim() adn y limits set by facet_wrap(...,scales="free_y")
messages.body_plain:
I do not understand the interaction of xlim() and the y limits that are automatically set by facet_wrap().
For example:
require(ggplot2)
mt <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
mt + facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free_y")
mt + xlim(c(15,30)) + facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free_y")

In the second plot, why does the y axis of the 3rd cell ("8") go up up to 5.5 if there are no points there?  Are not all points outside the x limits of c(15,30) being set to NA by xlim() ?

I've been given the solution of filtering out the data, which does produce the plot I need:

mt <- mtcars %>%
  filter(mpg>=15, mpg<=30) %>%
  ggplot(aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
mt + facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free_y")
mt + xlim(c(15,30)) + facet_wrap(~cyl, scales = "free_y")
But this is kind of inconvenient and, above all, I wish to understand why the plot using xlim() only is not the same as the one
using filter()

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Line 18 reads: Data points outside the limits are considered to be `NA`.

So setting xlim() is equivalent to
 mtcars %>%
  mutate(mpg = ifelse(mpg < 15 | mpg > 30, NA, mpg) %>%
  ggplot(aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free_y")

The corresponding y values are still available and hence used to calculate the range of y axis.

messages.subject: Re: Interaction of xlim() adn y limits set by facet_wrap(...,scales="free_y")
messages.subject_clean: Interaction of xlim() adn y limits set by facet_wrap(...,scales="free_y")
messages.body_plain:
ok, I understand it now thanks to your last statement:

> "The corresponding y values are still available and hence used to calculate the range of y axis."

But please note that this not the same than your first statement:

> "Line 18 reads: Data points outside the limits are considered to be `NA`."

This statement implies that both x and y coordinates would become NA, as a point is defined by both x and y. If you set a point to NA,
you set both x and y to NA because a point on a plane is a 2-tuple. The question is that what xlim() actually does is not setting the "point" to NA, but just its x coordinate, as you say in your last sentence. With that I understand ggplot behavior.

I have to add though that this behavior of xlim() is very counter-intuitive, if not illogical. If the user sets xlim(c(15,30), it is because he/she does not want to see points
within that range, so automatic y limits should adapt in accordance. Or at least this should be an option, sort of na.rm=TRUE.

Thanks a lot for your time,

Agus

messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to add the length of each segment using geom_step()? Below is some code that get's me the desired output, however I have to manually add the text labels, which will not work for multiple charts due to time constraints. Appreciate any feedback!

ex <- structure(list(Type = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C"
), Hz = c(50, 550, 1050, 800, 300, 50, 550, 1050), Vert = c(500,
500, 550, 600, 600, 700, 750, 700)), row.names = c(NA, 8L), class = "data.frame")

ex <- ex %>% arrange(Hz) %>%
  mutate(HzText= abs(Hz - lag(Hz, default = first(Hz)))) %>%
  arrange(Hz)%>%mutate(VtText= abs(Vert - lag(Vert, default = first(Vert)))) %>%
  mutate(HzMidpt= abs(Hz - lag(Hz, default = first(Hz)))/2+lag(Hz, default = first(Hz)))%>%
  mutate(VtMidpt= abs(Vert - lag(Vert, default = first(Vert)))/2+lag(Vert, default = first(Vert)))

ggplot(ex, aes(Hz,Vert, color=Type,group=1))+geom_step(color='black')+geom_point(size=5)+theme_minimal()+scale_y_reverse()+
  annotate("text",x=44,y=550,label='100',angle=90)+
  annotate("text",x=44,y=650,label='100',angle=90)+
  annotate("text",x=160,y=695,label='250')+
  annotate("text",x=300,y=650,label='100',angle=90)
